findings.title: Harmony hue-only selection prints angular degrees as the chosen matching metric
findings.evidence: When strictMatching=false on an HSV-carrying wheel, selector devianceFor returns angular hue distance (:139-141). executeHarmony assigns that value directly to the main row deltaE (:275), but companions get getDistanceForMethod (:278-280), and the card grades/formats every row under matchingMethod. Thus degrees are labelled and thresholded as DeltaE/OKLAB/RGB, mixing units within one result.
findings.repro: Run /harmony with strict_matching=false, companions=2 and matching=oklab on the RGB wheel. Inspect the main and companion row measurements: main is a hue-angle difference, companion is OKLAB distance. The former is graded against 0.041/0.101/0.174 harmony bands despite being degrees.
findings.test_gap: harmony.test.ts:365-389 tests only strictMatching:true and asserts result.ok, never the measures passed to generateHarmonyCard. No strictMatching:false case found in command tests. Static trace only; no suite/repro was executed by reviewer.
findings.fix: Keep hue deviance for selection, then recompute the selected dye row's displayed distance in matchingMethod just as for companions. Add a false-strictness card-argument regression; publish bot-logic then deploy consumers.

findings.title: Swatch merges same-index eyes even when live extended colors differ
findings.evidence: Swatch drops rightEye whenever eyesShareIndex and a leftEye row exist, and labels leftEye LR. The facade's flag is expressly index equality. Existing EXT-28 parity fixture has both indices 42, left offGrid #87C0A3 and right palette #DCBA6C while eyesShareIndex remains true. Those two distinct active colors therefore collapse into a single LR match; right color and its nearest dye disappear.
findings.repro: Pass EXT-28's shared-index/differing-floats document through executeSwatch (see parity fixture around :5669). Expect separate L/R rows because winning colors differ; current :427 skips R. slot:eyes also always selects the first collapsed row.
findings.test_gap: swatch-library.test.ts:358 tests shared indices only with left matchHex patched to null; ordinary shared-index tests use identical effective colors. Core parity proves the differing-color state but does not exercise command rendering. Static trace only; no suite/repro was executed by reviewer.
findings.fix: Merge only when both active winning hexes (including composites where relevant) are equal; derive the LR label from that effective-color equality. Add EXT-28 at the command boundary. Publish bot-logic, then deploy bot consumers.

findings.title: Character label cap can split a surrogate pair
findings.evidence: boundedLabel truncates raw UTF-16 at 256 code units. A 255-unit prefix followed by an astral character leaves a high surrogate without its low surrogate. producer and nickname projections both call this function; serialized/UTF-8 rendered nickname can show U+FFFD. SVG escapeXml drops illegal surrogates, so that sink does not break XML.
findings.repro: Import a .chara with Nickname = 'a'.repeat(255) + a supplementary-plane character. The capped nickname ends with only the first UTF-16 code unit of that character.
findings.test_gap: chara-library.test.ts:196-205 bounds only ASCII n.repeat(400) and asserts length 256, so a split supplementary-plane character is untested. Static derivation only; no suite/repro was executed by reviewer.
findings.fix: Truncate on code-point boundaries while preserving a documented code-unit cap; coordinate with web file-name truncation. Publish core before consumers.
findings.overlap: 2026-10-26-security/SECURITY_AUDIT_REPORT.md G67 (informational handoff); coordinator also owns web-app chara-file-loader.ts filename slice. Merge into one cross-unit item if filed.
findings.qualification: Cosmetic malformed boundary: the web card displays labels; SVG strips lone surrogates. Web file-name slice at apps/web-app/src/services/chara-file-loader.ts:89 needs the same boundary rule in its separate consumer sprint.

findings.title: Glamour embed truncation leaves oversized notes unbounded
findings.evidence: The 4000-character budget truncates only body. Names in fixed/blocked/company notes can make tail itself exceed that budget. The computed lastIndexOf position then becomes negative; with no newline at index zero, lastIndexOf returns -1 and body.slice(0,-1) retains almost the whole body. Description at :613 still includes the entire tail and can exceed Discord 4096 characters. The injectable resolver accepts long names and the live upstream cleanName has no cap, though abnormal game data is needed for the production scenario.
findings.repro: Use a resolver answer with a fixed/blocked/company name long enough that notes.join(newline) exceeds 4000 characters. executeGlamour returns ok:true with embed.description longer than 4096; ordinary body truncation cannot make an already oversized tail fit. Static derivation; reviewer did not execute this repro.
findings.test_gap: glamour.test.ts:624-660 covers long acquisition/body lines (BUG-127), keeping all closing notes short. It asserts the aggregate length only for that case; no oversized-note or negative remaining-budget case exists in the reviewed tests.
findings.fix: Allocate a nonnegative tail budget first and bound/compact note names or lines, then truncate body within remaining space and assert the final description cap. Add oversized-tail and no-complete-body-line cases. Keep the worker failed-edit handling as its separate finding.
findings.overlap: 2026-10-26-security SECURITY_AUDIT_REPORT.md G37 informational handoff; uncapped upstream names also intersect security FINDING-002. This candidate concerns library embed budgeting, separate from worker safeEditOriginalResponse outcome handling.

findings.title: Concurrent last-slot submissions can both be rolled back while consuming daily quota
findings.evidence: After both calls pass a cap-1 precheck, both INSERT presets and append-only events. Each postcheck counts every event, observes cap+1, and deletes its own preset/votes, but not its event. No insertion-order tie-break on submissions although reserveDailyEvent uses one.
findings.repro: At 9/10 events, synchronize two different valid palette requests so both recordSubmissionEvent calls complete before either postcheck. Both return 429; neither palette survives; effective count is 11 until midnight.
findings.test_gap: tests/handlers/presets.test.ts:688 mocks one overshooting request and asserts preset/vote DELETE statements; no second request or surviving append-only event assertion.
findings.fix: Reserve submission quota atomically or use the event's monotonic id as the final-slot tie-break and release reservations for rolled-back creates.
findings.overlap: Related to 2026-10-26-security/FINDING-018 (pre-reservation Perspective work), but this candidate concerns false rejection and consumed quota.

findings.title: Changing only the primary category can retain that category in secondary_categories
findings.evidence: validateEditRequest receives only current primary; if PATCH has category_id but omits secondary_categories, undefined is passed to validator and accepted. updatePreset retains old secondary_categories.
findings.repro: Existing primary=jobs, secondary=[zones]. PATCH only category_id=zones. Stored primary and secondary both contain zones.
findings.test_gap: tests/handlers/presets.test.ts:2975 sends both lists; :3001 tests an explicitly repeated primary; :3059 tests supplied secondary against unchanged primary. No promotion with omitted secondary list.
findings.fix: Validate effective primary plus effective secondary list after merging edits with the stored preset; optionally normalize away the promoted secondary.
findings.qualification: Category SQL uses OR/EXISTS and does not double counts; this is a stored/UI invariant defect.

findings.title: New-preset response reports vote_count 0 after the author's auto-vote is committed
findings.evidence: createPreset returns vote_count:0. The handler awaits addVote, which recomputes stored vote_count, then returns the original preset object rather than submittedRow or refreshed count.
findings.repro: Submit a new approved preset; POST response preset.vote_count=0 while immediately reading that preset yields 1.
findings.test_gap: tests/handlers/presets.test.ts:552 success case checks status, success, name and moderation_status at :606-610; no returned vote_count or DB-state comparison.
findings.fix: Build the response from the post-vote row already read for notification or copy the successful vote result's count.

findings.title: Concurrent preview replacements and preset deletion leave uploaded R2 objects orphaned
findings.evidence: Upload reads previousKey before image work and overwrites the row unconditionally, deleting only that stale key. Two uploads starting from A store B/C and both delete A; whichever loses its row reference is never removed. UPDATE changes=0 after concurrent preset deletion is also treated as success.
findings.repro: Synchronize two uploads after both read A; complete B then C. Row points at C, A deleted, B remains indefinitely with no DB reference. Or delete preset between read and UPDATE: upload returns success and stores an unreferenced image.
findings.test_gap: tests/handlers/presets.test.ts:1865 uploads sequentially (:1895), missing overlapping old-key reads. presets-quotas.test.ts:1160 covers thrown UPDATE, not successful zero-change UPDATE. preview-revision.test.ts covers moderator key binding, not author upload/delete CAS.
findings.fix: Compare-and-set against captured image state, inspect changes, remove newly stored object on lost/deleted row, and clean only the replaced key for the winning update.

findings.title: Favorite list can exceed Discord's embed description limit for legal preset names
findings.evidence: All 50 favorites are joined into one description with no total budget. Legal 50-character names can expand to 100 characters after markdown escaping; sanitizePresetName permits 100. HTTP rejection returns false and this adapter ignores it.
findings.repro: Favorite 50 distinct legal presets whose 50-character names contain underscores. Sanitized names alone can exceed 4096 characters before numbering/categories; edit fails.
findings.test_gap: preset.test.ts has no favorite-list cases. Add a 50-entry escaped-name case asserting <=4096 description and handling failed edit.
findings.fix: Paginate or budget complete lines within 4096 including escaped names and truncation notice; check edit success.

findings.title: Favorite listing still fans out up to 50 individual preset API reads
findings.evidence: Promise.all calls getPreset once per favorite, each a separate signed service-binding request and row query. Oct4 OPT-003 remains OPEN and current implementation is unchanged.
findings.repro: 50 favorites produce 50 getPreset/PRESETS_API.fetch calls; capped batch can reduce to one request/set query.
findings.test_gap: Add 50-entry call-count benchmark after batch endpoint exists. No runtime benchmark performed.
findings.fix: Deploy a capped approved-only batch-by-id API first, then switch the caller while preserving order, missing IDs and failures. Up to 49 fewer service-binding requests/query round trips per 50 favorites; not 49 fewer rows read. Coordinate the same implementation with security FINDING-024.
findings.overlap: Supersedes 2026-10-04-deep-dive/OPT-003 (OPEN). Same fan-out is security FINDING-024 because userless reads bypass limiters; schedule one fix.

findings.title: Favorite list presents transient API failures as permanently removed presets
findings.evidence: getPreset returns null for 404 and throws for 429/5xx/network errors; list catches all as null. All transient failures produce allRemoved; partial failures silently omit existing favorites and reduce displayed count.
findings.repro: Nonempty favorites and PRESETS_API returns503 for everyGET. List sends allRemoved and no upstream outcome mark.
findings.test_gap: preset.test.ts has no favorite-list cases. Add all503 and mixed found/404/503 outcomes.
findings.fix: Preserve found/missing/failed outcomes; show and trace upstream failures; identify partial results.
findings.overlap: Oct4 BUG-047 fixed autocomplete persistence; this separate list-response path still swallows transient errors, without writing KV.
findings.qualification: No KV mutation or permanent favorite deletion occurs.

findings.title: Glamour adapter records failed Discord edits as successful commands
findings.evidence: safeEditOriginalResponse catches HTTP/network errors, logs and returnsfalse. Glamour adapter awaits but ignores boolean, so no throw reaches catch/outcome handling. Trace with no mark defaultsok although deferred result was never delivered.
findings.repro: Have editOriginalResponse return HTTP400/429/500 after successful generation. Adapter resolves; failed edit logged but trace outcome staysok and user has no result.
findings.test_gap: Add glamour adapter test with safeEdit resolvingfalse and assert failure telemetry and usable fallback/retry policy. glamour.test.ts:16 mocks safeEdit=true; :147 asserts generated payload, without a false delivery case.
findings.fix: Check safeEdit boolean and mark delivery failure; select bounded retry or short fallback. Consider a shared delivery helper to prevent repetition across adapters.
findings.overlap: Security G37 explicit non-security handoff. Separate from package-owned oversize embed tail: distinct fix/deploy unit.
findings.qualification: The failed edit is logged; the incorrect success is command outcome accounting. An expired token may prevent recovery.

findings.title: SWAP does not cancel an export sheet still waiting for its chunk
findings.evidence: openSheet captures listSource and sheetOpenToken before import(). show(null), reached by SWAP, clears the visible file and actions but neither increments the sheet token nor checks the captured session in the import callback. The old character's export sheet opens after the chunk arrives. Dedicated source-level Vitest probe passes while asserting this observed defect; see repro-web.txt and scripts/repro-web.test.ts.
findings.repro: Load a glamour, click Copy list while its chunk is cold, then SWAP before the chunk arrives. The file is cleared but the old file's sheet still opens.
findings.test_gap: Existing lifecycle guards cover destroy/repeated opens; the audit's separate deferred import probe demonstrates the missing session-clear guard.
findings.fix: Invalidate sheetOpenToken and close any open export sheet on session replacement/clear, or bind the pending open to the captured session identity. Test SWAP and a replacement file during the import.

findings.title: Non-default match metrics lose units and precision in exports and swatch summaries
findings.evidence: ExportEntry carries only a delta number and no matchingMethod; describeEntry always renders DeltaE plus toFixed(1), and JSON writes deltaE rounded to two decimals. Extractor, gradient and mixer forward distances from the currently selected metric unchanged. For OKLAB, e.g. 0.024 becomes DeltaE 0.0 in CSS/SCSS/Tailwind, and 0.004 becomes numeric 0 in JSON. The matching metric is not supplied in the export metadata, so exported measures also cannot be interpreted reliably. Swatch selection sentences independently round the same method-dispatched distance to one decimal (:1938/:1943), while reverse badges use two (:1045); generic Delta alone is not asserted to be a false DeltaE label.
findings.repro: Select OKLAB and a source color with nonzero nearest-dye distance below 0.05; export from Extractor, Mixer or Gradient. Commented output reports DeltaE 0.0, while the core metric vocabulary specifies three OKLAB decimals. A swatch with such a match also says the dye sits 0.0 away. Use a distance below 0.005 to expose JSON rounding to zero. Static trace only; no runtime repro executed.
findings.test_gap: shared/__tests__/palette-export.test.ts:38 uses only delta 3.42; :53 pins DeltaE 3.4 and :96 pins deltaE 3.42. No method field or small OKLAB value is exercised. Components reviewer supplied swatch precision sinks; reviewed tests do not establish method-aware summaries.
findings.fix: Carry matchingMethod through export payloads, preserve its identity in JSON and format with the core metric vocabulary/precision (BAND_METHOD_DP gives OKLAB three places). Use the same precision in swatch summaries and reverse badges. Keep generic Delta labels where intended but identify the selected metric nearby.
findings.overlap: Component reviewer independently identified swatch-tool precision drift and left it for this combined candidate. Earlier 2026-10-04 palette-export local-date finding is unrelated and already fixed.
findings.qualification: Current v4-result-card has a dedicated DeltaE2000 readout; this finding does not claim that readout is a native OKLAB distance. Core BAND_METHOD_DP and Gradient/Mixer metric views establish the native precision rule.

findings.title: A delayed vote check can repopulate invalidated cache after a vote succeeds
findings.evidence: The shared request() helper snapshots cacheGeneration and refuses to cache answers spanning an invalidation (:292/:314), but hasVoted bypasses that helper and unconditionally caches its response at :559. voteForPreset/removeVote invalidate presets and delete vote:<id> when successful (:457-458/:509-510). A check initiated before that mutation can finish later and reinsert the old has_voted and vote_count for five minutes. The component generation guard avoids applying that late result immediately, but reopening the detail calls hasVoted again and receives the stale cached answer.
findings.repro: Hold an authenticated GET votes/p/check returning the pre-vote false state; complete POST votes/p successfully; then release the old GET. Close and reopen the preset detail within five minutes. It shows the pre-vote button/count from cache, even though the successful POST response had already updated it. Equivalent sequence exists for removing a vote. Static asynchronous trace only; no runtime repro executed.
findings.test_gap: services/__tests__/community-preset-service.integration.test.ts:445-457 covers in-flight getPresets answers across invalidatePresets()/clearCache(), but not hasVoted. Its hasVoted cases :288-342 check ordinary success/failure/authentication. preset-detail.ts:696-700 has a tested component generation guard for BUG-026, which hides the immediate overwrite but does not protect the service cache on reopening.
findings.fix: Snapshot cacheGeneration (and preferably authenticated identity) when starting hasVoted, and cache only if unchanged when its response arrives; invalidate on vote mutations/auth changes. Add a deferred check-versus-successful-vote test that verifies a subsequent hasVoted actually fetches fresh state.
findings.overlap: Related to earlier BUG-026 component race and BUG-031 list invalidation fixes, but this is their remaining service-cache resurrection path. Not a duplicate of BUG-108 failed-check count clearing.
findings.qualification: Distinct from fixed 2026-09-16-deep-dive/BUG-026 (component guard), 2026-10-04-deep-dive/BUG-031 (list cache) and BUG-108 (failed-check count).

findings.title: A language switch empties settled Swatch matches and disables Share
findings.evidence: The locale subscriber calls inherited update(), which renders a fresh matchResultsContainer and a fresh disabled share button. renderRightPanel ends by updating selection card, empty state, grid and handoff only. updateColorGrid never calls updateMatchResults or updateShareButton, and Swatch has no onUpdate override. selectedColor and matchedDyes survive but their cards do not. A pending price completion can accidentally repopulate cards, so use a settled selection with prices off.
findings.repro: Pick a swatch cell with market prices off and observe match cards plus enabled Share. Switch language. The selected cell/selection sentence remain, but cards are gone and Share is disabled. Pick a cell again to restore them.
findings.test_gap: swatch-tool.test.ts:1162-1169 rerenders only a loaded character card; :1324-1335 checks slot naming; :2027-2035 checks listener cleanup after update. None asserts forward matches and share state survive update. No suite was run by this reviewer.
findings.fix: Restore the derived match cards and share parameters during/after every render without reloading the selected cell or duplicating subscriptions; add a settled forward-match locale regression.
findings.overlap: Oct4 BUG-021 covered Harmony/Mixer/Comparison/Accessibility; this is the same failure class in Swatch, absent from that finding scope. Those four have restorative onUpdate paths today.

findings.title: A completed preset edit can dismiss a different modal
findings.evidence: showPresetEditForm discards the ID returned by ModalService.show. The form remains closable and Cancel remains enabled while editPreset/upload/remove awaits. Success then calls dismissTop(), so cancellation followed by another modal causes the old completion to dismiss that unrelated top modal.
findings.repro: Start a valid edit against a delayed response. Cancel the edit, open another modal, then resolve editPreset successfully. The newly opened modal is dismissed by the original edit completion.
findings.test_gap: preset-edit-form.test.ts:268-289 uses a deferred edit but checks only busy/restored button labels; it never closes the form and opens another modal before resolving. No suite was run.
findings.fix: Keep the edit form modal ID and dismiss only that ID, mirroring the submission form. Keep the callback semantics explicit when the initiating modal has already closed.
findings.overlap: Oct4 BUG-102 was the submission form and is fixed there using state.modalId. This independently surviving edit-form call is not that fixed source path.

findings.title: Accessibility ignores saved canonical display options until a setting changes
findings.evidence: Accessibility initializes cardDisplayOptions from DEFAULT_DISPLAY_OPTIONS and never reads getConfig(accessibility). Its subscription only handles future broadcasts; ConfigController.subscribe merely registers a listener and does not replay current state. The sidebar loads current canonical options, so persisted showHex=false/showRgb=false/showCmyk=true disagree with cards after entering/reloading the tool. Legacy vision-type restoration does not restore these card options.
findings.repro: Change global color-format options on another tool (for example hide HEX, enable CMYK), then enter Accessibility or reload on it and select a dye. Sidebar switches show saved settings, but cards use default HEX/CMYK visibility until another display toggle broadcasts.
findings.test_gap: accessibility-tool.test.ts:772-787 validates merging an explicit post-mount setConfig call. It does not preseed ConfigController, mount, and inspect first-render card properties.
findings.fix: Seed Accessibility display options from ConfigController before the first results render, then subscribe to changes. Retain intentional tool-specific metadata restrictions.
findings.overlap: Oct4 BUG-022 fixed first-render dye filters in four other tools; it did not cover Accessibility display options.
findings.qualification: Scope is supported display fields only; intentional Accessibility price/acquisition restrictions remain valid.

findings.title: Harmony ignores canonical harmony type on initialization and reset/import broadcasts
findings.evidence: The constructor restores selectedHarmonyType and companionDyesCount from legacy keys. onMount reads canonical harmony config but omits both of those fields. The controller subscription updates companions but never selectedHarmonyType. Direct sidebar type edits appear to work because the separate config-change bridge calls setConfig; resetAllConfigs/importConfigs broadcast without that bridge. Sidebar/serialized settings then say complementary (or imported type), while tool rail, wheel and results retain the legacy/current type.
findings.repro: Choose Triadic, open Advanced Settings and reset settings; return to Harmony results. The canonical/sidebar type is Complementary, but the results/rail remain Triadic. A fresh mount after importing a different type similarly reads the old legacy type. Companion count may initially disagree until a future harmony broadcast.
findings.test_gap: harmony-tool.test.ts:999-1029 tests direct tool.setConfig(type) and legacy writes; later controller regressions exercise wheel/market. They do not reset/import canonical type and compare sidebar, rail and output.
findings.fix: Use the canonical harmony config as the initial authority for type/count, and apply harmonyType through the controller subscription with the existing pin-clearing and regeneration behavior. Avoid redundant full regenerations from the bridge.
findings.overlap: Old sidebar controller mirroring BUG-027 is fixed in ConfigSidebar.mirror; the remaining tool-side omission is distinct.
findings.qualification: The sidebar mirror intentionally emits no config-change bridge event (config-sidebar.ts:748); direct sidebar edits do not prove reset/import works.

findings.title: Comparison ignores the global Stain and Spectrum display switches
findings.evidence: Comparison setConfig applies the five color formats, delta and price only. It never assigns showStain or showSpectrum. Both card render paths read optional fields with ?? true, so those rows remain enabled despite the visible global switches and canonical config becoming false. An exact-source method extraction confirmed setConfig({displayOptions:{showHue:false,showStain:false,showSpectrum:false}}) leaves all three current properties true.
findings.repro: On Comparison select one or two dyes. Turn off Stain and Spectrum in Options. Both switches remain off, but cards still show the stain readout and spectrum row. Navigate away/back: those fields are still default-on in the tool.
findings.test_gap: comparison-tool.test.ts:425-443 merely calls setConfig and asserts leftPanel has children. It does not inspect rendered card properties or rows, and its fixture omits the new options.
findings.fix: Apply the complete supported DisplayOptionsConfig key set, preferably through the shared helper. Seed it from canonical settings and test the single-card and duel-card rows.
findings.overlap: Different from 2026-10-04-deep-dive/BUG-039 (api-worker rate-limit tests) and 2026-09-16-deep-dive/BUG-039 (merge-test quality); neither covers these Comparison switches.
findings.qualification: Only Stain/Spectrum are claimed. Comparison's deliberate acquisition and pair DeltaE rows remain unchanged.

findings.title: Palette-driven Gradient and Comparison selections do not request their prices
findings.evidence: Gradient updates interpolation for endpoint picks, pins and algorithm changes without fetching prices; its only calls to fetchPricesForDisplayedDyes are in market-config handlers at :637/:649. Comparison.addDye, used by selectDye from the live v4 drawer, updates cards/results/storage but never fetchAndUpdatePrices. Its old embedded-selector listeners do fetch, but the v4 palette route does not use them. With prices enabled before selection and cold cache, the displayed price rows stay empty until a market/display change triggers a fetch.
findings.repro: Enable market prices, then select new Gradient endpoints or select Comparison dyes from the app-wide drawer while cache is cold. Observe no new price request and blank rows. Changing server/toggling prices causes them to load. Gradient restored selections have the same omission.
findings.test_gap: gradient-tool.test.ts:1266-1275 proves server changes refetch after a ramp is mounted, not the ramp-selection trigger. comparison tests selectDye for selection logic and price tests exercise legacy MarketBoard relays, not a cold-cache v4 selection.
findings.fix: Have the canonical results/selection-change path fetch the newly displayed dyes when price display is enabled, respecting existing service request coalescing and price toggles; cover direct v4 selectDye plus restored Gradient endpoints.
findings.overlap: Oct4 BUG-086 fixed the AND visibility gate; both toggles are on in this reproduction. Mixer mixing-field clicks at mixer-tool.ts:1408-1423 also rerank without their usual fetch, but that sibling is not required for this candidate.
findings.qualification: Exclude restored/shared Comparison selections, which explicitly fetch. The finding covers live v4 Comparison picks and Gradient recomputation/restored endpoints. DyeSelector.setSelectedDyes emits no selection event, so it supplies no indirect fetch.

findings.title: Preset card keyboard handling hijacks its Save and Vote buttons
findings.evidence: The focusable article handles every bubbling Enter/Space keydown, unconditionally prevents default and selects the preset. Its nested Save/Vote buttons stop click propagation only. A keyboard activation on either button reaches the article first; it opens details and cancels the button activation. An exact-handler JSDOM probe produced selectedDetail=1 and defaultPrevented=true for Enter dispatched on the child Save button.
findings.repro: Tab to Save or Vote on a preset card and press Enter or Space. The detail opens instead of saving/voting. Mouse clicks stop propagation and work normally.
findings.test_gap: preset-card.test.ts:214-243 checks face-button visibility/labels; no keydown coverage exists in the file. The probe exercised the actual extracted handler with DOM bubbling, not a full browser or suite.
findings.fix: Handle article keyboard activation only when the article itself is the event target, or use a separate open-details button so nested controls retain native keyboard behavior.
findings.overlap: Oct4 BUG-028 fixed the global dye picker keyboard path; this is the separate nested preset-card action path.
findings.qualification: Correct test path: apps/web-app/src/components/__tests__/v4/preset-card.test.ts:214. Independent verification used static native event semantics; the worker's extracted-handler DOM probe is not a full browser run.

findings.title: Arming an empty Gradient End slot still writes the picked dye into Start
findings.evidence: Clicking the End endpoint arms slot 1 and selectDye forwards that slot to setEndpoint. For an empty selectedDyes array, setEndpoint ignores idx and stores [dye], which is Start. An exact-source method probe of setEndpoint(1,dye) returned [dye] with startDye populated and endDye null. The dense-model comment explicitly says always fills Start first, so the coordinator should reconcile that legacy model rule with the new armed-slot UI contract before filing.
findings.repro: Clear Gradient, click its empty End card, then pick a dye in the palette. Start fills while End stays empty, despite End being armed.
findings.test_gap: gradient-tool.test.ts:1509-1545 exercises slot replacement/swaps with a complete existing ramp, never End-first on an empty tool.
findings.fix: Either represent a pending End endpoint independently so an armed pick goes into End, or prevent/clearly explain End arming until Start is selected. Preserve serialization and existing no-duplicate rules.
findings.overlap: Oct4 BUG-094 handled result-card swaps when both ends exist; those guards now work. This is the empty-selection branch and is marked design-contract-sensitive.
findings.qualification: Confirmed UI promise: enabled TO button and tooltip Click to select end color at gradient-tool.ts:929/934 and en.json:493. Preventing or explaining empty End arming can fix the contract while retaining the dense model; no sparse-model redesign is required.

findings.title: Editing a preset refreshes the public pool but leaves Mine and its edit baseline stale
findings.evidence: The edit-success callback invokes loadPresets only. Mine renders userSubmissions, and opening the edit form resolves its baseline from that same array. It is populated at connection/sign-in and refreshed after deletion or My submissions modal actions, but not after this direct detail edit. After successful edit, Mine can still show the previous title/dyes and reopening Edit uses the old values until another submissions refresh/reload.
findings.repro: From Mine open an owned preset and edit its name or dyes successfully. Return to Mine: its card still uses the old data. Reopen its Edit form: it is initialized from stale userSubmissions. Contrast delete success, which explicitly refreshes both sources.
findings.test_gap: preset-tool.test.ts covers Mine first loading at :1321-1350 and votes/history, but contains no edit-success refresh assertion. No suite was run.
findings.fix: Refresh or update userSubmissions on successful edit in addition to the public pool, including pending moderation fields, and assert the next Mine card/edit baseline reflects the authoritative response.
findings.overlap: No matching current security/dead-code item found; this is distinct from modal ownership wcomp-002.
findings.qualification: showTab at preset-tool.ts:1006 refreshes Community/Official only. Owner-visible edited values change even if moderation is pending, so Mine's stale baseline is observable.
